stem_book: A particle of mass m is suspended vertically from a vertical line AB at a distance (3√3/8)L from O as shown in figure. The object is given a horizontal velocity u = √(7gL/2). At some point, its motion ceases to be circular and eventually the object passes through the line AB. At the instant of crossing AB, its velocity is horizontal. When the particle leaves the circular path its velocity vector is (a) √(gL/8)(−î + √3ĵ) (b) √(gL/2)(−î + √3ĵ) (c) √(gL/2)(−√3î + ĵ) (d) √(gL/8)(−√3î + ĵ)
reason: key c has magnitude √(2gL) and wrong direction; leaving point is 30° above horizontal with v = √(gL/2) along (−1/2, √3/2) ⇒ option a (also reproduces the AB distance 3√3L/8)
